paragraphs: Plymouth City Council runs its own not-for-profit fostering service, Foster for Plymouth, and children in the city's care also live with carers from independent agencies such as those shown above.

During Foster Care Fortnight in May 2025 the council said 534 children were in its care, while Foster for Plymouth had 119 fostering households and 32 kinship carers, family or friends looking after a child they already know. When there are not enough homes nearby, it explained, children may go to a residential home or to a foster family outside the city, away from their school, friends, family and the professionals they trust. That is the reason it gives for asking more local people to come forward.

Two schemes launched in February 2025 show the kind of carer the city most wants. Emergency carers take children at short notice for up to two weeks and need a bedroom kept free at all times; the council added extra support for them, including an additional payment when a child arrives out of hours. Step Forward is for children with higher needs who could leave residential care for a family home in or near Plymouth. It asks for experience of children with complex needs, whether from fostering or from work in social care, health, education, youth justice or residential care, and offers a dedicated team with mental health practitioners, a buddy and a monthly support group.

Foster for Plymouth also recruits for time-limited and permanent fostering, respite, and parent and child care. You need to be over 21 with a spare bedroom; the council says renting, living in a flat, being single, having a disability, keeping pets, working or being retired are not barriers. Eligible carers can have their council tax covered, even if they live outside the city and foster Plymouth children, and there are extra payments for birthdays, a festival and holidays. We do not yet have a Plymouth pay page, so ask the service for its current rates.

Fostering with the council means caring for Plymouth's own children with its team behind you; an agency approves and supports you itself and looks after children for councils across the South West. Talk to Foster for Plymouth and to two or three of the services above before you choose. If you live outside the city, see our pages for Devon, Cornwall and Torbay.
